set.approach: The road up Death Canyon is seasonal, so the approach is on skis or snowshoes from the Moose-Wilson Road closure. In early season, go up to the Phelps Lake side, leave the maintained trail after two switchbacks and bushwhack to a log bridge over Phelps Creek, then follow the obvious forested drainage to the base. In mid-winter the frozen lake can be crossed instead, watching for avalanche paths. The flow is the prominent waterfall directly east of the Apocalypse Couloir, visible from the Phelps Lake Overlook. The base sits under that very large avalanche path and the gullies above the second pitch can slide, so check the avalanche forecast.
set.descent_text: Parties rappel the line from the anchors, going straight down the flow so the rope reaches as far as possible, and carry small nuts, pitons and cord to rebuild worn anchors. Knot the rope ends because they can reach the snow. If the fourth pitch is climbed, it has its own rappel anchor at the far right of the flow.

review.notes: Approach: log bridge/forested drainage from route page and the trip account; midwinter lake crossing and avalanche from the route page. Descent from the route page only; no counts given on purpose.

set.approach: The road up Death Canyon is seasonal. The usual way follows the Moose-Wilson Road south from the closure, takes summer trails to the east end of Phelps Lake and crosses the frozen lake into the canyon. Leave skis near the end and walk the last stretch to the base. The gully is a south-facing couloir on the north side of the canyon, beside the Sentinel turret on its west side, with the Cathedral Rock summer routes to the other side, almost opposite Prospector Falls. It can slide from above and below, and the sun reaches it from late morning, so check the avalanche forecast.
set.descent_text: Parties get down the main flow by V-thread rappels and downclimb the short first pitch. Fixed anchors cannot be counted on, so carry a V-thread tool and cord.

review.notes: Approach from the route/area pages and the trip account (Phelps Lake crossing). Descent: both the route page and the account use V-thread rappels; no counts.

set.approach: Natural Bridge is a short drive north of Dubois, reached on a seasonal road that a 4WD can follow to the canyon rim in light snow; once drifts close it, the rest is a ski tour or snowmobile ride. From the rim an obvious trail drops to the top of the bridge, and the east end is reached by turning right there and using a semi-technical descent on fixed ropes. The climb is the leftmost vertical ice and the first vertical ice met when arriving from the east. Stay on the access road across private land unless the landowner permits otherwise, and wear a helmet: hanging ice overhead is the main hazard.

review.notes: Approach is the area page's access and descent-to-the-bridge text; route position from the route's own page. Single source, no counts. No descent stated.

set.approach: Leave the Phelps Lake trail at its switchback, keep high on the hillside and sidehill across steep ground; the climb is a short way up from that traverse. The slopes crossed are steep and can hold avalanche debris, so check the avalanche forecast. The route faces south and starts on a low ice step.
set.descent_text: Parties can walk off by climbing a short way, heading left and descending back to the base. No rappel anchors are in place; a top-rope is set by slinging a tree at the top.

review.notes: Single route page; no counts used.

set.descent_text: From the top of Tower 1 the way down is the broken south-facing slabs on the back side, with rappels as needed to reach a couloir. Rappel slings are fixed at intervals but the old webbing may need replacing, so carry sling material. From the couloir, downclimb or rappel to the base.

review.notes: Descent from the route page only; the route ends on top of Tower 1 by a final rock pitch. No approach source beyond 'obvious from the basin', so approach left out.

set.approach: Follow the Glacier Trail deep into the range to its junction with the Wind River High Route, then continue a short way south to the cirque below the Sunbeam and Heapsteep faces. The route starts at the foot of the north face and climbs the whole Heapsteep Glacier first.
set.descent_text: The route finishes with two easy rock pitches to the summit. From there walk down the east ridge to Blaurock Pass.

review.notes: Approach from the area page, distances omitted (single source). Descent from the route page.

set.approach: Near the start of the Moraine camping zone in Garnet Canyon, turn north and head up between Glencoe Spire and Teepe Pillar. A long snow slope leads to the base of the gully. Steep snow slopes here are avalanche terrain, so check the avalanche forecast.
set.descent_text: The chute leads up to the Black Dike and Teepe Col. From the col, the way down is the Teepe Glacier.

review.notes: Single route page; descent stated for this route as via the Teepe Glacier. No counts.

set.approach: Reach Indian Basin and pick up the Indian Basin trail, then head toward the southeast watershed of Fremont Peak above the high lake and scramble up to the bowl in the Jackson and Fremont cirque. Expect off-trail travel across boulderfields, snow and lakes. From the bowl the couloir begins to the east and climbs northwest. Snow conditions vary a lot; check the avalanche forecast.
set.descent_text: The couloir finishes in one of the summit fingers and a short ridge and third-class scramble reach the top. Descend by the standard third-class Southwest Slope.

review.notes: Route page only; elevations and counts omitted. The route is on the Indian Basin side of Fremont Peak.

set.approach: The approach is the one used for the rest of the Cirque of the Towers; from camp in the cirque it is a short walk to the base of the Watchtower's east buttress, just south of the cirque lake. The line is the central, northeast-facing couloir: follow the highest snow to its top at the base of the buttress. Protection is scarce on the snow above the ice, so check the avalanche forecast.

review.notes: Location from the route page, access from the area page. No descent stated.

set.approach: From the Cabin Creek trailhead at the end of the South Fork road, cross the South Fork Shoshone River and pick up the trail on the far side. Follow it upstream past the Wilderness sign to the Love Canal drainage on the left. Continue through the forest to where the drainage pinches into a canyon, then hike or scramble up the frozen creek bed to the foot of pitch one.

review.notes: Approach from the route page, agreeing with the area page on the river crossing and trail upriver. Descent from the route page.

set.approach: From the Cabin Creek trailhead at the end of the South Fork road, cross the river by the usual crossing, turn right and follow the trail upriver. The flow is in a hidden spot up the creek on the right, directly across from the third pitch of Spyin' 'n Flyin' and a few minutes beyond where the trail crosses that creek.

review.notes: Route page location plus area page access. No descent stated.

set.approach: From the Cabin Creek trailhead at the end of the South Fork road, cross the river toward High on Boulder, then turn right onto the South Fork trail and head upriver. A prominent box canyon appears on the right and the route is on its left wall. The first pitches start by the river, so parties rappel in.
set.descent_text: Parties rappel from the top of the second pitch into a narrow slot that reaches the river inside the box canyon, climb out, cross the trail and continue up. Higher on the route a walk-off exists on the skier's left, and the lower pitches are rappelled from trees using V-threads or slings on vegetation.

review.notes: Route page; area page agrees on the river crossing and upriver trail. Distances omitted (single source).

set.approach: Park at the end of the road, hike past the ranch to the river and stay on its right side, either along the river or on game trails up the hillside. Two drainages run down the hillside nearly to the river; take the right-hand one.
set.descent_text: Descend by rappelling from trees, with V-threads or new slings where needed.

review.notes: Route page; area page agrees on parking and trail up the river.

set.approach: Park at the end of the road and take the trail past the ranch toward the river. Rather than crossing, stay on the faint trail along the north bank, and after a few minutes you reach a slight bench above the river. Two drainages climb from the bench; Grandma's Chicken is in the left one and Smoked Turkey in the right. Take the left fork a short way to the base. The route follows a deep slot in the rock.

review.notes: Route page; area page agrees on parking and the trail up the river. No descent text on the page.

set.approach: Park at the end of the road, hike past the ranch to the river and stay on its right side, then take the right-hand of the two hillside drainages to the base of Smoked Turkey. Drumstick starts by climbing the first two pitches of Smoked Turkey; it is the steep ice in the amphitheater just right of that route's third pitch.

review.notes: Start position from Drumstick's own page; the walk to the base of Smoked Turkey is from that route's page, which the Drumstick page names as the start. No descent stated.

set.approach: Hike upstream from the Cabin Creek trailhead past the Spyin' 'n Flyin' drainage and a little farther along the trail. Go down a bare rib until it ends, veer right through the forest, drop to where you can double back beneath the cliffs, and walk upstream a few minutes to the base. The river must be crossed; an ice bridge may exist, otherwise wading is needed. From the far side, scramble up rolling ice to the first pitch.

review.notes: Route page; distances omitted (single source).
